evidence.head_shape: All five figures' heads read as round near-circles under their hair volume (side-part brown, curly-updo/bun brown, black afro, blonde curly-updo, side-part brown), matching SEED's round bald-head-under-hair silhouette and base.png's round head doctrine. Confirmed via 3x head crops of all five figures.
evidence.no_nose_no_ears: PASS, round 2's regression is fixed: verified via 3x close-up crops of all five heads (cand_fig0..4_head_zoom.png) -- on every figure, hair (side-part fringe, curly-bun stack, afro, blonde curls) runs unbroken down to jaw/neck level with no separate ear shape, no ear outline, and no inner-helix/tragus line anywhere on any head. No nose is drawn on any figure (flat skin plane between eyes and mouth, identical to SEED's treatment, which also omits nose entirely). Clean pass, all five figures, no exceptions found.
evidence.four_digit_hands: Checked crops of hanging/visible hands on figures 0 (both hands), 2 (both hands) and 4 (both hands) -- representative sample across skin tones and poses (cand_fig0_lhand_zoom.png, cand_fig2_lhand_zoom.png, cand_fig4_rhand_zoom.png). Each shows the same simplified stylized mitt as SEED (seed_fig0_lhand_zoom.png, seed_fig4_rhand_zoom.png): 2-3 finger-separation notches reading as three-to-four fingers plus an implied thumb lobe, single dark outline, no five-digit realistic hand, no individuated fingernails. Matches the base rig hand family exactly.
evidence.proportion: QUANTITATIVE MEASUREMENT, two methods, both cross-checked against SEED (refs/base/crowd-exemplar.png), throwaway PIL scripts (measure_r3.py, measure_r3b.py) deleted after use per instructions. Method A (hair-inclusive silhouette height/head-width, noisy due to hats/hair volume): candidate figures 0-4 height=518,532,528,533,520px headW=184,207,197,207,182px ratio=2.815,2.570,2.680,2.575,2.857 (spread 2.57-2.86, range 0.29); SEED figures 0-4 height=493,523,585,523,493px headW=167,217,201,217,168px ratio=2.952,2.410,2.910,2.410,2.935 (spread 2.41-2.95, range 0.54, inflated/depressed by top-hat on fig2 and bonnets on figs1/3 -- not a body-proportion signal). Method B (face-fill-color head width, excludes hair, the reliable metric): candidate head_width=139,133,140,132,139px (tight, range 8px) with face_top=301-308, chin=428-466; SEED head_width=141,132,140,133,141px (tight, range 9px) with face_top=266-314 (fig2 depressed by top-hat pushing crown up), chin=428-445. Candidate and SEED head-width numbers match near-exactly per figure-position (139~141, 133~132, 140~140, 132~133, 139~141), confirming both images share the same underlying head/face construction scale. Method C (the decisive check per the retry brief -- leg span via 1.0x/1.5x/2.0x head-width gridlines drawn up from each figure's floor line, saved as candidate_gridlines.png / seed_gridlines.png plus 10 per-figure zoom crops cand_fig0-4_zoom.png / seed_fig0-4_zoom.png): for the three trousered men (figures 0, 2, 4 in both candidate and SEED), the jacket/vest/sweater hem -- i.e. where visible leg fabric begins -- lands right at or fractionally above the 1.0x (red) gridline in EVERY one of the six figures (candidate fig0 jacket hem at red line, fig2 jacket hem at red line, fig4 sweater hem at red line; SEED fig0 vest hem at red line, fig2 breeches/sock boundary at red line, fig4 jacket hem at red line) -- i.e. visible leg span is ~1.0 head-width or less in both sets, no daylight between candidate and SEED. For the two skirted women (figures 1 and 3 in both), the skirt in both candidate and SEED extends nearly to the floor (skirt hem sits below the 1.0x/red line in all four cases, with only shoe-tips visible beneath), so the 'exposed leg' comparison is moot -- both sets use full-length skirts identically, no leg-lengthening tell in the candidate that SEED doesn't also show. Ruling PASS: round 2's diagnosed failure (jacket/vest hem sitting at the 1.5x line, ~50% over ceiling, on trousered figures) is not reproduced anywhere in round 3 -- every trousered figure in the candidate now lands at ~1.0x, matching SEED figure-for-figure, and the skirted figures are visually identical in construction to SEED's skirted figures.
evidence.flat_cel_render: Flat single-colour fills across all five figures' skin tones and garments (jacket, cardigan, skirt, suit, tie, sweater-vest, sweater, jeans) with simple two-tone cel shading (one light panel, one darker shadow panel, e.g. right side of figure 0's jacket, underside of figure 1's cardigan sleeve) -- no gradient/airbrush blending and no random mottled/noise texture on any garment, confirmed via close crops (cand_fig0_jacket_zoom.png, cand_fig1_garment_zoom.png). EXPLICIT RULING on the tweed-style jacket on the leftmost figure (figure 0, brown corduroy-look blazer): the vertical striping is a set of evenly-spaced, uniform-width, straight parallel line strokes running with the fabric grain -- clean vector-style construction lines denoting a pinstripe/corduroy pattern -- not randomized pixel-level weave/mottle/noise (which would show irregular speckling and inconsistent line width/spacing). This reads as sparse clean construction lines and PASSES; it is the same category of device as the pleat lines on figure 1's and figure 3's skirts, which also pass.
evidence.outline_consistency: Even medium-thick dark outline is held across all five figures at consistent weight -- heads, hair, garments, hands and shoes all carry continuous unbroken outline with no thin or missing segments, matching the outline weight seen on SEED and base.png. No figure shows a thinner or heavier outline than its neighbors.
evidence.crowd_face_simplification: PASS: every one of the five figures has plain dot eyes (no highlights, no eyelids, no eyebrows), one simple neutral closed mouth line, no nose, no ears (see no_nose_no_ears), no teeth, and no individuated features distinguishing any one figure's face treatment from another's -- confirmed via the same five head-zoom crops used for no_nose_no_ears. Matches SEED's blank-face treatment exactly aside from the intentional restyle (hair/skin-tone/dress) that is this retry's actual mandate.
